strings.name: John Martinis
strings.summary: Trained at Berkeley, Martinis helped demonstrate macroscopic quantum tunnelling and energy quantisation in circuits, then developed superconducting processors at UCSB and Google. His team’s 2019 sampling advantage claim did not establish general practical computing advantage. He co-founded Qolab and shared the 2025 physics Nobel with Clarke and Devoret.
strings.influence.rationale: Advances superconducting quantum circuits and quantum computing experiments, contributing to research from fundamental physics to programmable quantum processors.
strings.facts.f1.value: San Pedro, Los Angeles, California, USA.
